newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cacique to import roasted Indian coffee.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cacique to import roasted Indian coffee.

text.p: Brazil's Companhia Cacique de Cafe Soluvel is importing 20,000 bags of roasted coffee from India to be re-exported as soluble coffee, said Elcio Martiniano, raw materials planning and purchasing manager.
The company is importing the coffee because of more attractive prices on the international market than in the domestic Brazilian market and is paying $67 per 60-kg bag cif.
The shipment should arrive in the next three to four weeks, Martiniano said.
In addition, Brazilian Soluble Coffee Association (ABICS) is co-ordinating the purchase by several firms of roasted coffee from various origins to be brought in one vessel, he said.

Representatives from across Brazil's coffee sector have for several months been discussing the problems facing the domestic soluble coffee industry which risks losing competitiveness due to higher internal prices for beans than in the world market.
The government has recently started including coffee in its monthly auctions specifically for the soluble industry but the quantity so far has been relatively small.
"It is regrettable the government with its 13 million to 14 million bags of stocks has forced us to take this position," Martiniano said.
In the last auction on April 2, the soluble industry bought all the 25,915 bags on offer at prices ranging between 59.50 reais and 71.50 a bag for green coffee.
In 1996, total Brazilian exports of soluble coffee were 58,000 tonnes, down almost four percent from the 60,365 tonnes exported in 1995. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
